slides.title: The architect's loop for AI systems
slides.text: Session 1 The architect's loop for AI systems Describe the architect's loop and where an AI system adds steps to it Separate drivers, constraints, concerns and assumptions in a brief Name the stakeholder who owns each concern 01

slides.title: Architecture is a loop from drivers to decisions, then back
slides.text: The architect's loop Architecture is a loop from drivers to decisions, then back 1 · Drivers goals, constraints, concerns → 2 · Scenarios targets with numbers → 3 · Options three, costed → 4 · Decisions recorded, with triggers → 5 · Review tested against scenarios Views are drawn all along the loop. A review that finds a failed scenario sends you back to step 3, not to a slide tool.

slides.title: An AI system adds four attributes a classic design rarely names
slides.text: What changes for AI systems An AI system adds four attributes a classic design rarely names Answer quality Correctness varies by question type, language and model version. Cost per request Tokens make cost a function of each prompt, not of a server count. Data in prompts Every prompt is a data flow to wherever the model runs. Human oversight Some answers must go to a person, by design. What goes wrong. These four are discovered after launch, by a complaint, a bill or a data protection officer.

slides.title: One ministry, nine product teams, one shared platform
slides.text: The case study One ministry, nine product teams, one shared platform 9 product teams on Asas, the shared AI platform 3 classification levels in use: Public, Restricted, Secret 38,000 building-permit applications a year The Ministry of Municipal Services is fictional and its data synthetic. Days 1 and 2 architect Muyassir, the building-permits assistant; Days 3 and 4 design Asas itself.

slides.title: Drivers, constraints, concerns and assumptions need different handling
slides.text: Sorting what people say Drivers, constraints, concerns and assumptions need different handling Kind What it is From the Muyassir interviews What you do with it Driver A goal the system exists for Median permit cycle from 21 to 10 days Turn it into a measure Constraint A decision already taken The permits system offers reads only Obey it; record its owner Concern A stakeholder's worry "Only an inspector can approve" Answer it with a scenario Assumption Believed, not checked Most questions cover 40 topics Test it before relying on it

slides.title: A concern without an owner is never closed
slides.text: Stakeholders A concern without an owner is never closed Owner Concern Sponsor No wrong requirement told to a citizen Inspectors The assistant must never sound as if it approves Applicants Know it is an assistant; reach a person Permit staff Logs must not rank their performance Permits team Traffic doubles after a fee change The owner signs the scenario When the inspectors' concern becomes a scenario with a target, the inspectors agree the target. That is how a concern gets closed.

slides.title: The constraint that matters most was said once, in passing
slides.text: The hidden constraint The constraint that matters most was said once, in passing Data protection officerApplicant files hold national identity numbers, deeds and site plans. They are Restricted, and they do not leave the Kingdom: not for storage, not for processing, not for a quick look by a model. Ruled out An external OCR service for deeds; an external model with applicant context; logs to an external dashboard. Still open A model hosted in the Kingdom; an external embedding of the published code.

slides.title: Five attributes carry most of Muyassir's risk
slides.text: Quality attributes for AI Five attributes carry most of Muyassir's risk Answer quality Share of correct answers, per question type and language Latency A percentile of the end-to-end time Cost Per answer, from tokens and the price card Privacy Answers that expose another person's data Human oversight Cases that must reach a person, and do And the classics Availability, security, modifiability stay

slides.title: A scenario has six parts, and the last one carries a number
slides.text: The scenario A scenario has six parts, and the last one carries a number Source an engineering office → Stimulus asks any question → Environment a normal working day → Artefact Muyassir via the gateway → Response a complete answer → Measure p95 ≤ 4,000 ms Testable. The measure names a metric that is recorded, a statistic and a target.

slides.title: "Fast, accurate and available" becomes three measures
slides.text: From the brief "Fast, accurate and available" becomes three measures The brief says The scenario measures Who measures it fast p95 of end-to-end latency ≤ 4,000 ms on a normal day gateway logs accurate share of correct answers to requirements questions ≥ 0.90 reviewers on a sample available at all times share of working-hours requests accepted ≥ 0.995 over a month the platform team What goes wrong. A target nobody measures. The lab's lint flags availability: the pilot never recorded it, so the platform team owes a measurement.

slides.title: Measure answer quality per question type, on a reviewed sample
slides.text: Answer quality is a number Measure answer quality per question type, on a reviewed sample A reviewer marks each pilot answer correct or not, against the building code. The scenario names the slice: requirements questions, 197 of the 400. Fee questions are 26 of 400: too few to claim anything about them yet. 0.92 correct on requirements questions in the pilot; target 0.90

slides.title: Human oversight becomes the share of cases that reach a person
slides.text: Oversight is a number too Human oversight becomes the share of cases that reach a person applicant Will my extension be approved if I move the stairs? rule approval question: only an inspector decides answer I cannot approve designs. An inspector can review it; shall I book a hand-over? 46 of 53 approval questions offered a person in the pilot Target 0.99. The pilot reaches 0.87: it fails.

slides.title: For privacy, count the leaks: a mean hides the one that matters
slides.text: Choose the statistic For privacy, count the leaks: a mean hides the one that matters 1 of 400 pilot answers showed another applicant's file (request P0288) Mean leak rate: 0.0025. It looks like success. Sum of leaks with a target of zero: it fails, as it should. One leak of a deed is a reportable incident, not a rate.

slides.title: Regulation as a design constraint
slides.text: Session 3 Regulation as a design constraint Classify a data flow by the highest level it carries Derive placement constraints from classification and transfer rules Find the flows a design must change 03

slides.title: Four levels, set by the impact of unauthorised disclosure
slides.text: National data classification Four levels, set by the impact of unauthorised disclosure Level Impact of disclosure In the Ministry Top Secret high none in this case Secret medium tender documents, land disputes, state land surveys Restricted low applicant files, status records, conversation logs Public none the published building code, fee schedule, zoning maps

slides.title: Open by default, highest level wins, classify at creation
slides.text: Three principles that shape designs Open by default, highest level wins, classify at creation Open by default Data is accessible unless its nature or sensitivity requires more protection. Highest level A dataset that combines levels takes the highest of them. A prompt is such a dataset. Timely Data is classified when created or received, so a new log needs a level on day one.

slides.title: Transfer abroad is a regulated path, not a hosting preference
slides.text: Personal data outside the Kingdom Transfer abroad is a regulated path, not a hosting preference Adequacy The competent authority publishes the countries and organisations that give an appropriate level of protection. Safeguards Otherwise, in set cases: standard contractual clauses, binding common rules or an accreditation certificate. Onward transfer The Law still applies when data moves on from the first recipient. For the architecture. Each flow that could leave the Kingdom names its path, or does not leave.

slides.title: Each level maps to where its data may be processed
slides.text: The Ministry's own rule Each level maps to where its data may be processed Level Ministry data centre Cloud region in the Kingdom External service Public yes yes yes Restricted yes yes no Secret yes no no Asas policy P-01. It is the case's rule, stricter by choice than the minimum the national texts set.

slides.title: A prompt is a data flow, and it takes the level of what it holds
slides.text: Prompts carry data A prompt is a data flow, and it takes the level of what it holds question Which documents are still missing from my application? retrieved clause 4.2 of the published code (Public) status read application record with identity number (Restricted) prompt level Restricted: the highest of its parts placement Ministry or a cloud region in the Kingdom only

F04 sends the published code to an external embedding model.

Transparency and explainability S14: citizens know it is an assistant; answers cite the clause. Accountability and responsibility Q5: approvals stay with an inspector, by measure.

slides.title: Two hops hold most of the time of a request
slides.text: One request traced Two hops hold most of the time of a request Answer model 2,900 ms Reranker 650 ms Status read 400 ms Retrieval 180 ms Portal, sign-on, gateway 160 ms p95 per hop, from the supplied hop measurements (synthetic). The log write is off the user's path.

slides.title: The request costs half its budget and runs 290 ms over its time
slides.text: The budget The request costs half its budget and runs 290 ms over its time 4,290 ms sum of p95s on the user's path; target 4,000 SAR 0.025 per request, from tokens and the price card; target 0.05 3,640 ms without the reranker for status questions

slides.title: A sum of p95s is an upper bound; check it against one measurement
slides.text: Reading a budget A sum of p95s is an upper bound; check it against one measurement Slow tails of different hops rarely meet in one request, so the sum overstates. Retries and queues add time no single hop shows, so the sum can also understate. The pilot measured 4,866 ms end to end: here the bound was not pessimistic. What goes wrong. A budget built from p50s. It fits on paper, and half the users wait longer.

slides.title: Which change can bring Muyassir under 4,000 ms?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which change can bring Muyassir under 4,000 ms? The sum of p95s is 4,290 ms: model 2,900, reranker 650, status read 400, the rest 340. Which single change most likely brings the p95 under 4,000 ms without a new model? Write the conversation log faster Tune the index for a faster median query Add a second gateway check before the model Skip reranking for status questions and send fewer clauses

slides.title: Patterns and when each fits
slides.text: Session 1 Patterns and when each fits Match a need to a pattern with fit questions Test a non-generative baseline on the same data as a generative one Explain when a classical model serves a need better 01

slides.title: Six patterns cover most of what the Ministry's teams ask for
slides.text: Patterns Six patterns cover most of what the Ministry's teams ask for Pattern Fits when A need at the Ministry Retrieval answers come from changing documents, with a citation permit questions from the code Agentic several steps whose order depends on results pre-check of a submission Fine-tuned a stable output form, high volume, thousands of examples standard inspection letters Classical a label from a fixed list, labelled data, speed and cost matter routing citizen reports Batch the answer is needed in hours, over many records nightly backlog summaries Event-driven something must happen when a record changes status-change notices

slides.title: Five questions choose the pattern before anyone names a model
slides.text: Choosing by questions, not habit Five questions choose the pattern before anyone names a model What is the output? A label, a cited answer, a document, an action. Are there labelled examples? Thousands change the options. Who is waiting? A person in seconds, a process in minutes, nobody until morning. How many steps, and does each depend on the last? How does the data change? Stable, weekly, live.

slides.title: Retrieval brings knowledge; fine-tuning shapes form
slides.text: A common confusion Retrieval brings knowledge; fine-tuning shapes form Retrieval The building code changes with each circular. Retrieval reads today's version and cites it. Updating means re-indexing, not retraining. Fine-tuning Inspection letters follow one house style. 9,000 approved letters can teach the form; facts still come from the inspector's notes. What goes wrong. Tuning a model on the code to "know" it: the next circular makes the model wrong and nobody can see where.

slides.title: Choose an agent only when the next step depends on the last result
slides.text: Agentic Choose an agent only when the next step depends on the last result task pre-check submission 2027-114 for missing documents step 1 read the forms: building type is a commercial extension step 2 so query the permits system for the fire-safety approval result approval missing output two documents missing, with the clauses that require them

slides.title: Batch and event-driven designs move work off the user's path
slides.text: When nobody is waiting Batch and event-driven designs move work off the user's path Batch Thirty district summaries a night: run them together at off-peak capacity, retry failures, and nobody sees a latency. Event-driven A status change publishes an event; a notifier reacts. 40,000 notices a month, and no applicant has to ask. Every status notice that is sent is a status call that is not made: the driver S02 is served by an event, not by a chat.

slides.title: APIs for questions, events for changes
slides.text: Integration APIs for questions, events for changes Interface Muyassir uses it for Design rule Read API of the permits system status of one application read only (S09); timeouts and a hand-over Status-change events notices to applicants at-least-once, so notices are idempotent Gateway API (OpenAI-compatible) every model call one door for credentials, quotas and audit

slides.title: For routing reports, a classifier beats the generative model
slides.text: Measured in Lab 2.1 For routing reports, a classifier beats the generative model On the same 600 test reports Accuracy Mean latency SAR a month, 95,000 reports Classifier, character n-grams 0.938 0.1 ms 0 Generative model (recorded) 0.908 1,340 ms 156 The classifier trains in seconds on a laptop processor; it is also right more often in Arabic: 0.951 against 0.903.

slides.title: Cost one option without a generative model, every time
slides.text: The non-generative baseline Cost one option without a generative model, every time It shows what the generative model must beat, in quality and in cost. It is the fallback when the model is down or over budget. Sometimes it wins outright, as for report routing. When it loses, say on what: for Muyassir, it answers 70% of questions against 92%.

slides.title: Three options, one of them without a generative model
slides.text: Muyassir's options Three options, one of them without a generative model O1 · Hosted in the Kingdom A model in a cloud region of the Kingdom, paid per token. Answers 92% of questions. O2 · Ministry-hosted An open-weight model on the Ministry's accelerators, paid per server. Answers 92%. O3 · Non-generative Guided search and a document checklist. Answers 70%. Prices are the case's synthetic ranges, not vendor prices.

slides.text: Total cost of ownership Five lines make a three-year cost, and the last one is often forgotten Line What it holds Moves with Build first year only scope Run and people platform fees, the team that operates it time Tokens requests × tokens × price volume and price Capacity units servers sized for the peak month peak volume, in steps Unanswered work questions not answered become calls volume and coverage

slides.title: At the base forecast, O1 costs least over three years
slides.text: Measured in Lab 2.2 At the base forecast, O1 costs least over three years Option Three years, SAR Per answered question Year-1 run, SAR O1 hosted in the Kingdom 6.25 million 1.08 1.40 million O2 Ministry-hosted 7.59 million 1.31 1.71 million O3 non-generative 11.92 million 2.71 2.27 million Year-1 run includes the calls from unanswered questions. Without them, O1 runs at about SAR 1.0 million, under the SAR 1.2 million cap.

slides.title: Volume moves O1's total by half; token price by 3%
slides.text: Sensitivity, one assumption at a time Volume moves O1's total by half; token price by 3% Volume high +58% Volume low -20% Token price ×2 +3% Token price ×0.5 -2% O1's three-year total against its base of SAR 6.25 million (Lab 2.2, step 4).

slides.title: The Ministry-hosted model wins only at high volume and double prices
slides.text: When would O2 win? The Ministry-hosted model wins only at high volume and double prices 900,000 requests a month, steady, at double the token price: O2 matches O1 At the base price there is no crossover below three million a month. The high forecast reaches 900,000 only in its last month. So the decision has a trigger: volume, then price.

slides.title: Show ranges and their sources, never one confident number
slides.text: Reading cost models Show ranges and their sources, never one confident number Every price has a source and the date it was read. Every volume has an owner who will defend it. Every option is costed with the same lines. What goes wrong. An options paper that costs the favourite option in detail and the others on a napkin. Reviewers spot it from the number of lines.

slides.title: Lock-in and exit
slides.text: Session 3 Lock-in and exit Price the exit of an option from its lock-in factors Find the weight at which a weighted ranking flips Write procurement requirements a reviewer can verify 03

slides.title: Lock-in sits in the data and the contract, rarely in the model
slides.text: Lock-in Lock-in sits in the data and the contract, rarely in the model Data Indexes and logs in a store with no bulk export Contract Minimum terms and early-exit fees Formats Prompts and tools in one provider's shape Evidence Evaluation sets kept only in a vendor console

slides.title: The cheapest option to run is the dearest to leave
slides.text: Measured in Lab 2.3 The cheapest option to run is the dearest to leave Option Exit cost, SAR O1 hosted in the Kingdom 540,000 O3 non-generative 357,500 O2 Ministry-hosted 322,500 Vector store, no export 250,000 Early-exit fee 167,500 Prompt formats 70,000 Evaluation in console 52,500 Person-months at SAR 35,000 plus fees, from the case's exit factors.

slides.title: Weights are opinions; report how far they can move
slides.text: Weighted criteria Weights are opinions; report how far they can move Double counting. Three-year cost and exit cost are both money; say so, or merge them. Ordinal scores. A 4 is not twice a 2; small score gaps are noise. Hidden weights. A criterion left out has weight zero, by decision. Rank reversal. Find the weight at which the leader changes, and print it.

slides.title: Weigh exit cost at 0.13 instead of 0.10, and O2 overtakes O1
slides.text: Measured in Lab 2.3 Weigh exit cost at 0.13 instead of 0.10, and O2 overtakes O1 4.20 O1's weighted score at an exit weight of 0.10 4.10 O2's weighted score at the same weights 0.13 exit-cost weight at which O2 leads A fragile ranking. A three-point change of one weight reverses it. The decision record says so.

slides.title: A procurement requirement keeps the exit open only if it can be verified
slides.text: Buying the exit down A procurement requirement keeps the exit open only if it can be verified WeakThe provider will make data available where possible. VerifiableThe provider shall export all indexed documents, their embeddings and metadata in JSON Lines or Parquet within 10 working days of a request, at no extra charge. Test the export once a year: request it, load it into the Ministry's index, re-run the evaluation set and record the time taken. Untested, the requirement is only paper.

slides.title: Replace a legacy system one capability at a time, behind a facade that routes
slides.text: Leaving in steps Replace a legacy system one capability at a time, behind a facade that routes Applicants one enquiry address → Facade routes each question by its capability → Muyassir status, fees, part of documents and setbacks → Guided search the rest, until retired Route by capability: move status questions, then fees, then documents, each on its own evidence. Keep the way back: rolling back is one route flipped in the facade, with no deployment. Retire in steps: a legacy part goes only after four weeks without traffic and once its rollback window has closed.

slides.title: A deviation is a decision record with an expiry
slides.text: Deviations A deviation is a decision record with an expiry Conditions Each with a number a reviewer can check. Residual risk In numbers, and who accepts it. Expiry A date, and the events that reopen it sooner. What goes wrong. A deviation without an expiry becomes the new standard by default, with nobody having decided that.

slides.title: Three things to keep
slides.text: Day 4 Three things to keep Paths, not documents A template with its gates on is a standard teams actually follow. Checks and reviews Checks catch what the file shows, every commit; a review asks whether the design is right. Bounded exceptions A deviation has conditions, a residual someone accepts and a date it ends.

AI-full. Any assistant was allowed in the repository; the questions are where you show the decisions are yours.

Record numbers, not a fresh opinion: the decision records whose triggers fire, and what each would become.
